what_its_for: Senna is a natural laxative used to treat occasional constipation (difficulty having a bowel movement). It works by stimulating the muscles in your intestines to help move stool through your body. It is also sometimes used to help clean out your bowels before a medical procedure.
how_to_take: Take senna by mouth with a full glass of water (8 ounces). You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. Swallow tablets whole. If using syrup or liquid, measure your dose carefully with the measuring cup or spoon that comes with the product. Do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Drink plenty of fluids (at least 6 to 8 glasses of water per day) while taking this medicine to help it work better.
dosing: Adults and children 12 years and older: The usual dose is 1 to 2 tablets (or 10 to 15 mL of liquid) taken once or twice a day. Do not take more than 4 tablets (or 30 mL) in 24 hours. Children 6 to 11 years: The usual dose is 1 tablet (or 5 to 7.5 mL of liquid) once or twice a day. Do not give more than 2 tablets in 24 hours. Children 2 to 5 years: Ask your doctor or pharmacist before use. Always follow the dose on the product label or as directed by your doctor. Do not use for more than 7 days in a row unless your doctor tells you to.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not double up to make up for a missed dose. Since senna is usually taken only as needed, a strict dosing schedule may not apply to you.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep the bottle or package tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking senna for longer than 7 days in a row without talking to your doctor, as long-term use can cause your bowels to become dependent on it. Avoid taking other laxatives at the same time unless your doctor approves. Do not take senna if you have stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or a sudden change in bowel habits that has lasted more than 2 weeks — talk to your doctor first. Avoid if you have a bowel blockage or appendicitis. Limit alcohol while taking senna, as it may worsen dehydration.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get medical help right away if you: have no bowel movement after taking senna for 3 days; have rectal bleeding or black/tarry stools; experience severe stomach pain, cramping, or bloating that does not go away; feel dizzy, weak, or very tired; notice a change in how much you urinate; have nausea or vomiting; or if you have been constipated for more than 2 weeks. Also talk to your doctor before using senna if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have any ongoing health conditions.
when_it_works: Senna usually causes a bowel movement within 6 to 12 hours after taking it. Some people may not see results for up to 24 hours. For best results, take it at bedtime so it works by morning.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Senna is sometimes considered safe for short-term use during pregnancy, but always check with your doctor or midwife before using it. Breastfeeding: Small amounts of senna may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before using it while breastfeeding. Older adults: Older adults should use the lowest effective dose and stay well hydrated to avoid dehydration or electrolyte imbalances. Children under 2 years: Do not use senna in children younger than 2 years old unless directed by a doctor.
